title: (No AI) David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/gettyimages-2274329497.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

During Paramount Skydance's [latest earnings call](https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/pijdt4q9/), CEO David Ellison said "it's hard to imagine" AI won't have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company's outlook for AI, Ellison said:

> "I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history. The last time we saw anything close to this was really the, you know, advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 90s. title: (No AI) What could China get from Jensen Huang?
author: Hayden Field
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/STKP210_JENSEN_HUANG_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

It's difficult to overstate Nvidia's power in today's AI landscape. The company's chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump.
